measures.id: Guilford County Local Sales and Use Tax Referendum
measures.title: Guilford County Local Sales and Use Tax
measures.summary: Asks whether Guilford County should add a local sales and use tax of one-fourth of one percent (0.25%) on top of all other state and local sales and use taxes. Per the ballot question, the revenue would be used only for classroom teacher salary supplements (70%), fire protection equipment and services (18%), Guilford Technical Community College (8%), and qualifying municipalities for allowable expenses (4%).
measures.yesMeans: An additional 0.25% local sales and use tax is levied in Guilford County for the listed purposes.
measures.noMeans: The additional 0.25% local sales and use tax is not levied.

measures.id: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Greensboro may issue up to $11,500,000 in parks and recreation bonds, under an order adopted August 3, 2026, to acquire, build, renovate, remediate, improve and equip parks and recreational facilities, including related land and equipment and financial assistance to other parties for those purposes. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $18,257,755 ($11,500,000 principal plus $6,757,755 interest) and the property tax increase needed to repay them at $2.80 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: Greensboro may issue up to $11,500,000 in parks and recreation bonds and levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: Greensboro may not issue these $11,500,000 in parks and recreation bonds.

If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: Greensboro may issue up to $15,900,000 in firefighting facilities bonds and levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: Greensboro may not issue these $15,900,000 in firefighting facilities bonds.

measures.id: City of Greensboro Transportation Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Greensboro Transportation Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Greensboro may issue up to $7,000,000 in transportation bonds, under an order adopted August 3, 2026, for transportation improvements such as streets, sidewalks, streetscapes, bridges, bicycle lanes, greenways, buses and bus station and shelter improvements, including related land and equipment. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $11,104,459 ($7,000,000 principal plus $4,104,459 interest) and the property tax increase needed to repay them at $1.70 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: Greensboro may issue up to $7,000,000 in transportation bonds and levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: Greensboro may not issue these $7,000,000 in transportation bonds.

measures.id: City of Greensboro Municipal Building Bonds Referendum

The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $3,329,922 ($2,100,000 principal plus $1,229,922 interest) and the property tax increase needed to repay them at $0.50 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: Greensboro may issue up to $2,100,000 in municipal building bonds and levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: Greensboro may not issue these $2,100,000 in municipal building bonds.

measures.id: City of Greensboro Housing Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Greensboro Housing Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Greensboro may issue up to $5,000,000 in housing bonds, under an order adopted August 3, 2026, to acquire, build, improve, rehabilitate and equip multifamily and single-family housing, principally for people of low and moderate income, including neighborhood revitalization, permanent supportive housing, and loans or grants to such persons and to housing providers. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $8,063,912 ($5,000,000 principal plus $3,063,912 interest) and the property tax increase needed to repay them at $1.20 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: Greensboro may issue up to $5,000,000 in housing bonds and levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: Greensboro may not issue these $5,000,000 in housing bonds.
